ecologyNotes:
Mycorrhizal, in Kentucky mostly with oak and beech on well-drained slopes. Fruits singly or scattered from soil and leaf litter, often over a wide patch, never in fused clusters and never from wood. The hymenium is not gills: blunt, forking, cross-veined ridges that run down the stem and cannot be cleanly peeled away from the cap flesh. Flesh is white throughout when cut, which is the one-second check against Omphalotus.

OPEN QUESTION FOR REVIEW: eastern North American 'chanterelles' are a species complex and Cantharellus cibarius sensu stricto is a European taxon. The Kentucky material is likely C. flavus / C. tenuis / C. spectaculus depending on habitat, and the smooth chanterelle C. lateritius (near-smooth hymenium, so hymenium.type would be 'smooth' and this set's first discriminator would behave differently) is common in the same woods. Decide whether v1 ships a single sensu lato entry or splits C. lateritius out — it changes the confusion set.

OPEN QUESTION FOR REVIEW: spore print is recorded here as 'white'. In the field it is pale yellow to cream. The controlled vocabulary has no cream; confirm 'white' is the right coarsening, or the vocabulary needs a value.
